 Apollo Micro Systems shares rally 9% as Q2 net profit jumps 56% YoY
 SECTIONS Apollo Micro Systems shares rally 9% as Q2 net profit jumps 56% YoY By Surbhi Khanna , ET Online Last Updated: Oct 26, 2026, 12:35:00 PM IST Rate Story Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis Apollo Micro Systems has reported an impressive rise in Q2 earnings, with net profit soaring by 56% compared to last year. Revenues spiked 72%, hitting a milestone of Rs 388 crore for the September quarter. The notable increase in EBITDA showcases solid operational efficiency in the defence sector. The company is dedicated to enhancing its capabilities and expanding into global markets, demonstrating a strategic focus on its future objectives.
 ET Online Shares of Apollo Micro Systems jumped nearly 9% on Monday to hit the day's high of Rs 410 on the NSE after the company reported strong year-on-year growth in its Q2 earnings , with net profit rising 56% and revenue surging 72%.
 In an exchange filing, the company said its net profit increased 55.6% year-on-year to Rs 48.4 crore in the September quarter, compared with Rs 31 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Revenue from operations rose 72.2% to Rs 388 crore from Rs 225.3 crore a year earlier.
The company said its Q2 revenue of Rs 388 crore was its highest-ever for a September quarter.
 Also Read | Kotak Mahindra Bank shares climb 4% after Q2 results. What are Jefferies, Goldman Sachs saying? 
EBITDA grew 87.6% to Rs 111 crore from Rs 59.2 crore. The EBITDA margin expanded to 28.6% from 26.3%. The profit after tax (PAT) jumped nearly 54% to Rs 46 crore which was the highest-ever Q2 PAT.
 Live Events
 The company had a total order book of Rs 1,765 crore, an all-time high. The total revenue from operations was reported at Rs 388.1 crore in Q2, whereas the other income was Rs 3.5 crore.
 The profit after tax margin (PAT Margin) went up 15% in the second quarter of FY27. On a year-on-year basis, the profit after tax went up to Rs 47.7 crore from Rs 33.1 crore in Q2FY26, registering a growth of 200% on a yearly basis.
 “Our best-ever Q2 performance reflects strong execution, resilience and an unwavering focus on key priorities. Building on this momentum, we will accelerate execution, sharpen our strategic focus and remain responsive to the evolving needs of the defence sector,” said Baddam Karunakar Reddy, Managing Director, Apollo Micro Systems.
“With significant opportunities ahead, we are committed to strengthening our capabilities, advancing national defence preparedness and delivering with greater speed, discipline and purpose,” Reddy further said.
Reddy also said that, “We have come this far through perseverance; we move forward with purpose, and we look to the future with the conviction that our greatest contributions may still lie ahead. Thank you for being an integral part of Apollo's journey and for continuing to believe in the vision we are building together.”
The company also shared its Vision 2036, which said that its vision is to grow as a Global Original Equipment Manufacturer over the next ten years with recognisable revenue streams across the Land, Air and Sea domains.
It also plans to increase its presence in Indian markets and continue to grow in global markets; delivering valued products built with conviction; and strengthening our Research & Development with the latest and most futuristic technologies.
The Hyderabad-based publicly-listed defence and aerospace technology company said that for H1 FY27, revenue stood at Rs 639.44 crore, EBITDA at Rs 164.91 crore and PAT at Rs 71.37 crore, registering year-on-year growth of 78.2%, 64.7% and 49.6%, respectively.
 Also Read | IndusInd Bank shares rise 2% after Q2 results. Why Jefferies cut target price despite lender swinging to profit 
 Apollo Micro Systems share price movement
In the last one month, the shares of Apollo Micro Systems went up marginally by 0.04%. In the current calendar year so far, the stock went up 43.39% and nearly 35.93% in the last one year.
The stock gained 436.25% in the last three years and nearly 3,285% in the last five years.
